title: Horse domestication at Botai, Kazakhstan
summary: In 2009 researchers reported three lines of evidence that people of the Botai culture of northern Kazakhstan domesticated horses about 5,500 years ago: leg-bone shape unlike local wild horses, bit-type wear on horse jaws, and mare-milk fat residues in pottery. That would make domestic horses about 1,000 years older than previously thought and about 2,000 years older than those in Europe.

uncertainty.note: The sources say "around 5,500 years ago" and "fourth millennium BC"; the year is a midpoint, not a date. The finding is a 2009 research claim.

as_recorded.value: around 5,500 years ago; the fourth millennium BC

where.modern_name: Botai, North Kazakhstan Region (pin on the village of that name; the sources place the culture in the steppe east of the Urals in northern Kazakhstan)
where.historical_name: Botai culture settlement area, steppe east of the Ural Mountains (Eneolithic; no polity)

importance.justification: Earliest reported evidence of horse harnessing and milking, central to the later history of the steppe.
